correctness.rationale: With U=gcd(A,C), divide it out to obtain coprime X,Y. Then X B=Y D gives B=VY and D=VX with a unique monic V. Squarefreeness of UVXY is exactly individual squarefreeness and pairwise coprimality of the four components; equal input degrees force component degrees (k,k,n-k,n-k). Unique factorization therefore gives one empty and four single-slot choices at each prime, and factoring off the four geometric series gives the stated H_q. A coefficient indexed by j contributes q^(2n)h_q(j) for each integer k from max(j1,j2) through n-max(j3,j4), including the degree-zero endpoints. On any common radius R<sqrt(q) the Euler product converges normally because all linear local terms cancel and the total bound on local deviations is a constant times sum_d (R^2/q)^d. At R=q^(1/4), Cauchy gives exponential coefficient decay q^(-|j|/4). Replacing the positive part by its linear argument only changes indices with |j|>n; using at most binom(m+3,3) indices of weight m and an O(m+n+1) multiplier proves the stated O_q((n+1)^4 q^(-n/4)) error. The two untruncated sums are H_q(1,1,1,1) and the displayed b_q. The leading product is positive since every factor is positive and the sum of squared prime reciprocals converges. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/audit_recompute.py 2` compared the exact positive-part coefficient identity to direct squarefree-product multiplicities in 19 cases: the 15 stated test cases plus four over F4. The frozen AUDIT.json count of 17 is a bookkeeping discrepancy, not a theorem failure; RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and the actual loop ranges specify 15. Finite checks do not prove the asymptotic.
